text.arabic_uthmani: وَلَوْ قَٰتَلَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوَلَّوُا۟ ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيًّۭا وَلَا نَصِيرًۭا

words.gloss_range: resumptive and coordinating conjunction that links the counterfactual scene back to the prior discourse
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does not open a detached scene. It carries the prior claim of divine capability into a new counterfactual case, so the unreal battle reads as an explanatory extension of 48:21 rather than a free-standing possibility. The payoff is a boundary move: one non-event, the unreached gain of 48:21, is followed by another non-event, the battle that did not occur, under the same divine arrangement.

topics.headline: resumed counterfactual link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the counterfactual battle is tied back to 48:21 instead of beginning as an isolated hypothetical.
topics.reason: QAC parses the particle as conjunction, and the local clause evidence lets it coordinate the law-clause with the preceding context while leaving counterfactual force to the next particle.

topics.headline: two non-events under one arrangement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the move from unreached territory to unrealized combat as a single boundary argument about divine arrangement.
topics.reason: The boundary rows connect the opening conjunction to 48:21's capability coda, and no guardrail evidence blocks reading the particle as carrying that transition.

words.gloss_range: counterfactual conditional particle marking an unrealized condition whose consequence is nevertheless asserted
words.prose: {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}) makes the fighting scenario unreal, not merely possible. Its scope holds the whole ayah together: hypothetical combat, certain rout, and then a delayed support vacuum. That counterfactual choice also distinguishes this scene from the open-condition pattern in 3:111, so 48:22 presents a battle that did not need to happen while still making its outcome grammatically secure.

topics.headline: unreal condition with secured result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the fight is explicitly unreal while the outcome inside that unreal frame is asserted as certain.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as counterfactual, and attachment evidence makes the following clauses its condition and answer sequence.

topics.headline: condition then rout then support vacuum
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the ayah as one staged conditional scene rather than as separate statements.
topics.reason: The local syntax forces a law-protasis, a marked apodosis, and a sequenced consequence; the CRITICAL rows preserve that architecture.

topics.headline: parallel made into proof-form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the 3:111 fight-backs-no-help pattern is recast here as an unreal proof of the prior capability claim.
topics.reason: The cited 3:111 contrast is concrete, and the boundary rows explicitly connect the counterfactual certainty to 48:21's capability and encompassment.

words.gloss_range: Form III direct combat against the addressed community inside an unreal condition
words.root_gloss_range: range includes killing and lethal conflict; local Form III narrows it to mutual fighting or combat engagement, not a prediction of slaughter
words.prose: {{ar:قَٰتَلَكُمُ}} ({{tr:qātalakumu}}) puts the addressed believers inside the threat by fusing the second-person plural object into the combat verb. The Form III shape narrows the broad {{ar:ق ت ل}} ({{tr:q-t-l}}) field from killing to mutual fighting, but it keeps lethal-stakes pressure: even full combat would end in enemy flight. The verb also front-loads action before the subject is fully identified, and its field echoes 48:16 and the fight-backs-no-help architecture of 3:111 while remaining counterfactual here. Its long opening cadence lets the combat threat press into the addressed battle theatre before the later retreat word compresses the outcome.

topics.headline: believers as direct combat target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the hypothetical attack aimed directly at the addressed community, not described at a distance.
topics.reason: The object suffix is syntactically forced as the direct object of the verb, and the fused surface makes the addressees part of the combat word.

topics.headline: mutual combat with lethal stakes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the ayah tests a reciprocal combat scenario, not a one-sided killing claim.
topics.reason: The root can include killing, but QAC and verb-form evidence identify Form III, which selects fighting or mutual combat in the local frame.

topics.headline: completed unreal combat condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah can assess the battle as if completed, while the action is named before the enemy class.
topics.reason: The perfect verb under the counterfactual particle stages a completed condition, and local word order places the combat relation before the relative subject.

topics.headline: combat field answered by rout and no help
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this combat word as part of a recurring fight-then-rout field, with 48:16 reversed and 3:111 reworked into counterfactual certainty.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete references at 48:16 and 3:111, and the local ayah carries the same combat-to-retreat sequence without letting those references override the local counterfactual parse.

topics.headline: heavy opening pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses the long heavy combat opening press into the addressed battle theatre before the retreat verb compresses the outcome.
topics.reason: The sound and boundary rows add a distinct local payoff: the threat becomes personal to the addressed community within the prior military geography.

words.gloss_range: masculine plural relative pronoun defining the enemy subject by the following clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) delays the enemy's full identity until the relative clause completes. The subject is not a vague hostile group; it is the class defined by the following act of denial. That makes the counterfactual defeat attach to a moral-grammatical category, not to ethnicity or a named faction alone.

topics.headline: subject defined by relative clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the fighters are defined by the following denial clause rather than left as an unnamed enemy group.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as a masculine plural relative pronoun and attachment evidence forces the following verb as its defining relative clause.

words.gloss_range: completed intransitive denial defining the relative subject, with no explicit object limiting the denial
words.root_gloss_range: range includes covering, denial, concealment, and ingratitude; local Form I intransitive usage selects denial as a defining posture while retaining the covering image as lexical pressure
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) completes the subject definition as a settled act of denial. Because no object is supplied, the denial is not narrowed to one named thing; the broad {{ar:ك ف ر}} ({{tr:k-f-r}}) covering-denial field remains a posture. The local irony is sharp: those characterized by covering are later pictured through exposed backs. Same-surah recurrence at 48:25 and 48:26 keeps this adversarial class active beyond the single counterfactual scene, and the clipped consonantal texture makes the enemy label feel abrupt and closed.

topics.headline: settled denial defines the subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees denial as the completed identity-marker of the fighters before the hypothetical battle is considered.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect Form I in the relative clause, and its plural ending closes the subject definition internally.

topics.headline: objectless covering-denial posture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that no explicit object limits the denial, so the word marks a broad covering-denial posture rather than one specified refusal.
topics.reason: The intransitive frame blocks choosing a single omitted object while the root evidence supports covering, denial, and ingratitude as the semantic range behind the local denial sense.

topics.headline: covering reverses into exposure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a semantic reversal: the covering-denial class becomes the group whose retreat exposes its backs and lacks support.
topics.reason: The rows connect the covering image to exposed backs and to support-denial contexts without making that image replace the local verbal sense.

topics.headline: abrupt denial label in surah thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a clipped enemy label that also links forward to later same-surah conflict at 48:25 and 48:26.
topics.reason: The sound row is locally tied to the subject label, and the same-surah references are concrete enough to preserve as a candidate payoff.

words.gloss_range: answer-lam prefixed to the apodosis, marking the guaranteed result of the counterfactual condition
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) is the hinge from unreal condition to guaranteed result. Because it is prefixed directly to the first apodosis verb, certainty arrives before the no-support clause: if the fight had happened, the first named consequence is already locked as flight.

topics.headline: answer-lam locks the apodosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact pivot where the unreal condition becomes a single guaranteed outcome.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the prefix as the answer-lam for the law conditional, and clause evidence forces the following verb as the apodosis.

topics.headline: one-letter pivot into result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the turn from condition to result compressed into one attached particle.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL row identifies the particle as the transition point from protasis to asserted consequence.

words.gloss_range: Form II completed turning-away or retreat in the counterfactual apodosis, governing the backs object
words.root_gloss_range: range spans nearness, governance, alliance, and turning away; local Form II with the backs object selects committed retreat while retaining a same-root reversal toward later absent patronage
words.prose: {{ar:وَلَّوُا۟}} ({{tr:wallawū}}) gives the first consequence as completed retreat. The Form II surface selects active turning away, not mere nearness, and the following object makes the motion bodily: they turn by exposing backs. The same {{ar:و ل ي}} ({{tr:w-l-y}}) family later names the absent patron, so the ayah makes one root carry both their withdrawal and the failure of protective nearness. The 3:111 and 48:16 echoes remain local contrasts: this is a counterfactual rout, not a reported battle. The doubled middle sound gives the apodosis a compressed snap from facing combat into withdrawal before the failed search for support begins.

topics.headline: completed retreat as first result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees battlefield collapse as the first finished consequence before the later search for support begins.
topics.reason: The perfect apodosis verb carries the same plural subject from the relative clause and precedes the delayed no-finding phase.

topics.headline: committed turning away
topics.reader_payoff: The reader pictures a committed physical pivot that exposes the rear, not a vague change of relation.
topics.reason: The w-l-y root has broader nearness and governance branches, but Form II plus the explicit backs object selects the retreat branch locally.

topics.headline: same root turns from flight to absent patron
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same root move from enemy withdrawal to the later absence of anyone who maintains protective nearness.
topics.reason: The root-family rows are coherent with the later support noun and do not require changing the local retreat sense.

topics.headline: recognized rout pattern recast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a known turning-backs defeat pattern, with 3:111 and 48:16 present as concrete contrasts.
topics.reason: The rows cite specific recurrence fields at 3:111 and 48:16, and the local counterfactual frame narrows their role to echo or contrast.

topics.headline: compressed retreat sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the apodosis snap from facing combat into withdrawal, then hand off to a failed search for support.
topics.reason: The sound and boundary observations add a local payoff without overruling the syntactic object relation.

words.gloss_range: definite plural backs as the accusative object of the retreat verb, forming a recognized rout image
words.root_gloss_range: range spans rear, aftermath, and managing consequences; local noun selects physical backs while carrying aftermath and loss-of-control pressure
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ}} ({{tr:al-adbāra}}) makes retreat visible as the object turned: the exposed rears become the scene's first landing point. The definite plural treats the backs as a known rout category, distributed across the enemy group. The {{ar:د ب ر}} ({{tr:d-b-r}}) range also lets rear shade into aftermath and management, but locally that pressure rides on the physical image rather than replacing it. The phrase belongs to a recurring turning-backs formula, including 3:111 and 59:12, here placed inside a counterfactual. Its open cadence at the end of the rout beat gives way to the later indefinite tanwin closures, matching the shift from exposed backs to denied support categories.

topics.headline: backs become the turned object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader pictures the rear itself exposed as the object of turning, not merely the subjects labeled as fleeing.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces the noun as the accusative direct object of the retreat verb, preserving the concrete object relation.

topics.headline: known collective rout image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a collective battlefield rout image rather than one individual's back.
topics.reason: The definite broken plural is locally coherent with the plural subject and the recurring rout idiom.

topics.headline: rear image carries aftermath pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that exposed backs also hint at exposed consequences and loss of control, while the local noun remains physical backs.
topics.reason: The root range supports rear, aftermath, and management, but the local object noun and attachment to the turning verb narrow the selected sense to the physical rear image.

topics.headline: formulaic rout closes first beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the military-collapse beat close on the known turning-backs formula before the support-collapse phase begins.
topics.reason: The formula rows are locally anchored in the exact verb-object phrase and include concrete recurrence references such as 3:111 and 59:12.

topics.headline: open cadence into negated support
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the rout image open into the later indefinite support denials, while distributional evidence keeps the form in a marked defeat field.
topics.reason: The cadence and distribution rows add local payoff by connecting the object to the later tanwin closures and to constrained rear-retreat usage.

words.gloss_range: delayed sequential conjunction moving from completed rout to the later no-support aftermath
words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) slows the consequence sequence. The ayah does not collapse flight and helplessness into one instant; after the completed rout comes a second phase in which the routed group keeps searching and finds no support. The hinge also shifts from perfect event to imperfect aftermath, so defeat widens from battlefield motion into network collapse under the prior encompassment of 48:21.

topics.headline: delayed support-failure phase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that helplessness is a second realization after rout, not simply the same moment restated.
topics.reason: QAC and clause evidence identify the particle as sequencing the no-finding clause after the apodosis.

topics.headline: from completed rout to ongoing search
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the grammatical pivot from a completed defeat to an ongoing failed search.
topics.reason: The particle stands between a perfect retreat verb and an imperfect finding verb, and the prosody row reinforces the held transition.

topics.headline: military collapse widens to support collapse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees battlefield defeat open into social and military isolation already precluded by 48:21's encompassment.
topics.reason: The boundary and structural rows connect the particle to the widening from rout to no patron and no helper.

words.gloss_range: negation particle governing the imperfect finding verb and opening the two-object support-denial frame
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) opens the aftermath as ongoing negated finding. Because the ayah uses this particle with the imperfect rather than a past- or future-bound negator, the support vacuum stands as a continuing condition inside the counterfactual. It also begins a frame that gathers both denied support categories under one search verb while the later repeated negation keeps the second category distinct.

topics.headline: ongoing support vacuum
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the denial as a continuing support vacuum, not only a single failed past discovery.
topics.reason: QAC parses the particle as negating the imperfect finding verb, and the CRITICAL row distinguishes it from past- or future-bound alternatives.

topics.headline: one search field, two denials
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one negated search field contains both support objects while the repeated rhythm keeps each denial audible.
topics.reason: The attachment translation support says the two objects remain in a coordinated neither-nor denial, and the prosody row adds the clipped negative cadence.

words.gloss_range: imperfect plural finding verb under negation, governing both denied support objects as an ongoing failed search
words.root_gloss_range: range includes finding, encountering, possessing, existence, and felt experience; local Form I keeps the routed enemies as searchers who cannot encounter or possess support, not creators of support
words.prose: {{ar:يَجِدُونَ}} ({{tr:yajidūna}}) turns the aftermath into a continuing failed search. The routed group remains the subject, and one verb governs both support objects, so patronage and active aid are tested inside the same search field. The {{ar:و ج د}} ({{tr:w-j-d}}) range broadens the failure from simple discovery toward encounter, possession, and available means, while Form I keeps them as searchers facing reality rather than agents who can bring support into being. The wording also points forward to finding-language in 48:23 and recalls the no-finding formula of 4:173. Against 48:21's encompassment, the failed search has no outside support-space in which a patron or helper could be encountered.

topics.headline: imperfect search after rout
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the consequence continue after the rout as an unresolved search that keeps failing.
topics.reason: The imperfect under negation follows the perfect retreat verb and gives the no-support clause continuing force.

topics.headline: one verb gathers both support objects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same routed deniers keep searching, and one verb gathers both denied support categories.
topics.reason: Implicit-subject evidence carries the denier group forward, and attachment evidence makes both support nouns objects of the finding verb.

topics.headline: finding as encounter and available means
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses that support is not merely unseen but unavailable as encounter, possession, or means, while the local form keeps the action as finding.
topics.reason: The root range supports encounter, possession, means, and existence, but the local Form I imperfect excludes making the enemies causative producers of support.

topics.headline: no-finding formula bridges to next ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees failed support-search in 48:22 turn into the findability of God's pattern in 48:23, with 4:173 as a concrete no-finding formula parallel.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete references at 4:173 and 48:23, and the local phrase shares the finding-plus-support-denial frame.

topics.headline: no outside location for support
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the failed search to 48:21's encompassment: there is no outside support-space for the routed enemies.
topics.reason: Boundary rows explicitly connect prior encompassment to unfindable support, and collocation rows keep the patron-search formula local.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative patron-protector noun as the first denied object of the finding verb
words.root_gloss_range: range includes nearness, responsibility, patronage, governance, alliance, and turning; local nominal usage selects a durable patron-protector relation under class-wide negation
words.prose: {{ar:وَلِيًّۭا}} ({{tr:waliyyan}}) names the first thing the routed enemies cannot find: not one known patron, but any patron-protector at all. The indefinite tanwin under negation makes the absence class-wide, and the fa'il-type nominal presents the missing support as a durable relation-holder. The {{ar:و ل ي}} ({{tr:w-l-y}}) family makes the reversal more pointed: after the same root has named their turning away, it now names the absent nearness-agent who would have responsibility, alliance, or protective management. As the first half of the patron-helper doublet, its tanwin cadence pairs with the final helper term while preserving the difference between structural patronage and active aid.

topics.headline: any patron denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the negation deny every possible patron-protector, not merely one expected ally.
topics.reason: The noun is indefinite accusative with tanwin under negation, which supports class-wide denial in the local finding clause.

topics.headline: patronage is explicitly searched for
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that structural patronage is the first explicit searched-for object before active aid is denied.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the noun the first object of the finding verb, and the order places relational support before the active-helper term.

topics.headline: nearness as responsible protection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the missing waliyy as responsible nearness, authority, and protective management, not only casual friendship.
topics.reason: The root range supports nearness, governance, and aid, while the local noun keeps the active sense to a patron-protector relation rather than the retreat verb branch.

topics.headline: turning away meets absent nearness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears one root carry both their motion away and the absence of anyone who stays near on their behalf.
topics.reason: The same-root echo between the retreat verb and the patron noun is locally present and does not require collapsing their distinct senses.

topics.headline: first half of support-denial doublet
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the patron term paired with the helper term as a comprehensive support denial, with shared tanwin cadence binding the pair.
topics.reason: The rows connect the word to the waliyy-nasir formula, the paired cadence, and 48:21's prior divine management as the boundary that preempts alternate patronage.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction linking the second negated support object to the first
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the second denied support term coordinated rather than appositional. The result is additive: no patron, and separately no active helper. By linking two related but distinct roles, the particle helps build a compact support-field collapse, with 48:16 in the background as a fight field now answered by flight and absent support.

topics.headline: two support roles kept distinct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that patronage and active help are coordinated as distinct losses rather than collapsed into one synonym.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the second object with the first, and the repeated negation later reinforces the additive structure.

topics.headline: fight field returns as support denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the fighting field of 48:16 reappear as a coordinated absence of support after hypothetical enemy flight.
topics.reason: The intertext rows cite 48:16 specifically, and the local conjunction helps complete the two-part support denial.

words.gloss_range: renewed negation before the second support object, making active aid independently absent
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) renews the negative force before the final support term. It is not just a tail on the first object; it separately empties the active-aid category, so no helper remains as a fallback after patronage has already failed. The repeated open syllable also makes the last denial land as a fresh closure.

topics.headline: active aid separately negated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that active help is independently denied, not swallowed into the prior patronage denial.
topics.reason: The second negation and conjunction create an additive neither-nor structure that keeps the final object distinct.

topics.headline: fresh negative closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final denial reset rather than trail off as an afterthought.
topics.reason: The prosody row gives a local auditory payoff for the repeated negation immediately before the final word.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative intensive helper noun as the final denied object, naming active aid or victory-support
words.root_gloss_range: range includes helping, supporting, rescuing, and giving victory; local fa'il-type noun selects a reliable helper-agent, denied class-wide under repeated negation
words.prose: {{ar:نَصِيرًۭا}} ({{tr:naṣīran}}) is the ayah's final removed possibility: not merely a known rescuer, but any active helper at all. The indefinite tanwin makes the denial class-wide, while the fa'il-type form names a reliable helper-agent rather than an abstract help event. The {{ar:ن ص ر}} ({{tr:n-ṣ-r}}) field carries aid and victory, so the enemy side is denied the very support-root that elsewhere marks victory in this surah at 48:3. Because this word closes the ayah, the final landing is not just flight but total support failure, in a recurrent retreat-no-help pattern also seen at 3:111 and 59:12. The active search for a helper, rather than a passive no-help wording, resolves the counterfactual as no route from battle to aid and prepares the divine-pattern statement in 48:23.

topics.headline: any active helper denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final denial universalize the active-helper class, not merely remove one expected rescuer.
topics.reason: The noun is indefinite under repeated negation, and the syntax places it as the separately denied second support object.

topics.headline: active aid inside same failed search
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes active intervention from structural patronage while seeing both inside the same failed search.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the second object of the finding verb, and the lexical rows distinguish active aid from the prior patron term.

topics.headline: victory-help as reliable agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the help-victory root denied as a dependable helper-agent, with same-surah victory resonance at 48:3.
topics.reason: The n-s-r range includes aid and victory, but the local fa'il-type noun selects the helper-agent rather than abstract victory itself.

topics.headline: retreat-no-help formula closes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 48:22 gather fight, backs, failed finding, patronage, and help into a compact retreat-no-help formula, with 3:111 and 59:12 as concrete parallels.
topics.reason: The recurrence rows identify the waliyy-nasir doublet and the defeat-to-no-help sequence, while the local counterfactual and finding-language make 48:22 distinctive.

topics.headline: final support-failure landing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah close on total support failure, with matching tanwin binding the final pair and active aid removed last.
topics.reason: Final position, paired tanwin, and synthesis rows converge on support collapse as the ayah's landing rather than a mere synonym after flight.

topics.headline: ending resolves the counterfactual
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the unreal fight resolved as no route from battle to aid, preparing the next ayah's statement of divine pattern in 48:23.
topics.reason: The rows connect the final no-helper wording back to the opening counterfactual and forward to the divine-pattern claim in 48:23.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The irrealis protasis at qatalakum leads to lawallawu al-adbar, then thumma opens a second phase with two coordinated negations.
baseline_models.mechanism: Reciprocal combat triggers forced reorientation and rear exposure; only after that visible rout does the retreating side try and fail to locate either affiliative protection or effective aid. The verse therefore stages military reversal and support collapse as linked but non-identical events.

activation_trace.role: The reciprocal-combat sense supplies the initiating confrontation between two sides rather than an isolated act of killing.
The turning-away sense makes the first consequence a loss of orientation and engagement.
Rearward exposure concretizes the turn as battlefield retreat and defeat.
Finding as actually encountering a sought object turns the support clause into a failed post-rout search.
Affiliative protection supplies the first missing layer of support after retreat.
Active assistance and being made to prevail supply the second missing layer of support.

changed_reading.before: A generic prediction that hostile fighters would lose and receive no help.
changed_reading.after: A two-stage causal sequence: mutual combat flips their orientation into exposed retreat, and the routed side then discovers that both protective affiliation and effective assistance have disappeared.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The same root, و ل ي, occurs in the verbal lawallawu and the nominal waliyyan on opposite sides of thumma.
baseline_models.mechanism: The first occurrence enacts withdrawal from relation; the second names the relation no longer available. Turning away is thus self-canceling: the movement that abandons adjacency and engagement culminates in the inability to find a near, loyal protector.

activation_trace.role: Withdrawal and refusal of engagement supply the action performed by the routed side.
Unbroken nearness supplies the relational condition that the turn destroys.
Loyal affection and support name the unavailable relation at the end of the chain.
Mutual back-turning and estrangement expose the social fracture latent in the physical retreat.

changed_reading.before: The verb 'turn' and the noun 'ally' function as unrelated vocabulary.
changed_reading.after: The repeated root makes the verse reflexive: their act of turning out of relation becomes the condition in which no sustaining relation can be found.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The coordinated but non-identical objects waliyyan and nasiran follow a single negated finding verb.
baseline_models.mechanism: Wali names near attachment, custodial standing, or loyal alignment, whereas nasir names intervention that actively helps or makes one prevail. The double negation maps a complete support failure across relationship and action rather than repeating one idea for emphasis.

activation_trace.role: Nearness without an intervening gap supplies the positional layer of a wali.
Standing over and managing an affair supplies the custodial layer of the missing wali.
Concrete assistance and prevailing over an opponent supply the action layer of the missing nasir.
A single failed search governs both support layers and makes their joint absence experiential.

changed_reading.before: Wali and nasir are a synonymous pair meaning 'helper.'
changed_reading.after: The routed side lacks both a relation that stays near and an agent that can intervene; belonging and efficacy fail together.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Al-adbar sits between the turn and thumma, allowing the rear or end of the event to become a temporal hinge.
baseline_models.mechanism: The backs are not only anatomy. The root also opens the event's latter end and consequence: combat gives way to retreat, retreat to a search, and search to recognized abandonment. This preserves a slower aftermath reading alongside the immediate rout reading.

activation_trace.role: The latter end and passing consequence of a thing extend al-adbar from body position into aftermath.
Attention to what an affair will lead to makes the exposed rear a gateway to the battle's outcome.
Uninterrupted succession supplies a root-level echo for the verse's chained consequences.
The later act of seeking and failing to encounter support closes the aftermath sequence.

changed_reading.before: The verse depicts one instantaneous battlefield collapse.
changed_reading.after: It also traces an aftermath in stages, from exposed rear to the eventual discovery that the social and operational field is empty.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah names opening and victory while repeatedly describing hands being withheld. That sequence revises the focus counterfactual from an anticipated battle report into a guarantee of capability whose actual historical force can operate through restraint: the enemy would rout if combat occurred, yet victory need not be identical with combat occurring.

activation_trace.role: Two-sided combat remains the unrealized condition against which the surrounding victory is measured.
Victory as an opening supplies a result category broader than battlefield collision.
Deliberate prevention of hands from acting supplies the first enacted restraint.
Reciprocal restraint of hands supplies the realized alternative to the focus verse's combat condition.
Prevailing is explicitly present before the reciprocal restraint, showing victory and non-fighting can coexist.

structural_cues: 48:22 is explicitly irrealis, while 48:24 narrates reciprocal restraint after prevailing.
Opening is announced at 48:1 before the focus verse supplies its unrealized combat test.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opening, withheld hands, and prevailing; I infer that these recode the battle counterfactual as assured but deliberately suspended capacity. A live alternative is that the restraint and the hypothetical rout describe separate episodes without redefining victory.

changed_reading.before: The verse primarily promises victory through a battle that is expected to happen.
changed_reading.after: The verse guarantees what combat would reveal while the surrounding sequence presents restraint itself as a mode of victory and opening.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier context materializes the support missing from the enemy side: divine aid makes the addressee prevail, and pledged hands form a bonded human network under the divine hand. The focus pair wali/nasir is therefore polarized against an already-built architecture of loyalty, authority, and intervention.

activation_trace.role: Loyal alignment names the relational support denied to the routed side.
Effective aid names the operative support denied to the routed side.
The doubled promise of aid supplies the positive pole against the focus verse's absent nasir.
The pledge of obedience turns affiliation into a binding collective relation.
The supporting-hand sense gives the pledged network a bodily image of assistance.

structural_cues: 48:3 positively repeats nasr, while 48:22 negates the availability of a nasir.
48:10 stacks hand over hands inside a covenant before 48:22 denies the opposing side both affiliation and aid.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies promised aid, pledged allegiance, and layered hands; I infer a distributed support architecture contrasted with the enemy's empty search. A live alternative is that covenant and battlefield aid remain separate motifs joined only by proximity.

changed_reading.before: The enemy simply happens to have no helper at the moment of defeat.
changed_reading.after: Their lack is systemic: they face a side whose nearness, covenant, authority, and active aid cohere, while no comparable support architecture remains available to them.

context_deltas.mechanism: In 48:16-17, turning away from a summons to fight is a culpable refusal; in the focus verse, hostile fighters themselves turn away under defeat. The repeated roots make physical withdrawal ethically role-sensitive: turning is not intrinsically condemned or praised, but exposes whether one abandons an obligation or loses an aggressive initiative.

activation_trace.role: The focus combat condition supplies the hostile initiative that will collapse.
Turning away supplies the shared motion whose value changes with the actor and obligation.
A summons to reciprocal fighting supplies the duty-setting counterpart to the focus counterfactual.
Repeated withdrawal from the summons supplies the culpable version of the same root movement.
The renewed warning fixes turning away as abandonment of commanded participation in this context.

structural_cues: 48:16 places fighting and turning away in one conditional sequence before 48:22 reverses which side turns.
The actor changes from reluctant members of the addressed group to the attacking disbelievers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the same combat and turning roots with different actors; I infer that role and obligation determine the movement's ethical force. A live alternative is simple lexical repetition without a designed reversal.

changed_reading.before: Turning the back is itself the verse's moral failure.
changed_reading.after: The focus turn is the forced reversal of aggression, set against an earlier voluntary abandonment of duty; identical movement reveals opposite relational failures.

context_deltas.mechanism: The holdbacks had imagined that the messenger and believers would never turn back to their families. The focus counterfactual reverses that forecast: the people expected not to return are secure, while the hostile side is the one whose orientation flips. The battlefield turn thus answers an earlier imagined irreversible disappearance.

activation_trace.role: The hostile side's turn supplies the reversal of the earlier forecast.
Return and changed destination supply the earlier prediction that the faithful group would not come back.
The circle of familial belonging supplies the destination the holdbacks imagined permanently lost.

structural_cues: 48:12 reports a confident prediction of non-return; 48:22 later assigns decisive turning to the opposing side.
Both passages concern group orientation under the prospect of combat.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an earlier failed forecast of non-return and a later counterfactual hostile turn; I infer narrative irony between them. A live alternative is that the two orientation verbs are not intended to answer one another.

changed_reading.before: The focus verse predicts only a future tactical maneuver.
changed_reading.after: The maneuver also overturns the holdbacks' prior map of who would disappear and who would return, converting their suspicion into narrative irony.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately following verse repeats a future-negated act of finding and makes its object the alteration of an established way. That echo turns the focus side's inability to find a wali or nasir from contingent battlefield scarcity into one manifestation of a stable, non-substitutable pattern.

activation_trace.role: The failed encounter with sought support establishes the first negated finding.
Unavailable loyal protection is the first concrete object governed by the invariant pattern.
Unavailable effective aid is the second concrete object governed by the invariant pattern.
The immediate repetition of finding under future negation carries the focus search into the next verse.
A continuously followed way supplies the stable process behind the particular rout.
Substitution by one thing for another supplies exactly what cannot be found in the established pattern.

structural_cues: 48:22 and 48:23 are adjacent and each contains a future-negated form of finding.
The second object, substitution of the established way, generalizes the first verse's unavailable support.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, repeated negated finding, and non-substitution; I infer that 48:23 lifts 48:22 from event to rule. A live alternative is that the repeated verb is local cohesion without a stronger causal generalization.

changed_reading.before: No ally or helper happens to be reachable after this particular rout.
changed_reading.after: Their failed search is the concrete enactment of an invariant order for which no substitute outcome can be found.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus denies any discoverable protector or helper once hostile combat begins, but the later account says combat was withheld while unknown believers remained intermixed and vulnerable to being trampled. Their unrecognized presence is not a wali or nasir for the hostile group; it is a hidden structural restraint that delays enactment of the focus outcome for everyone in the mixed field.

activation_trace.role: Failed finding anchors the contrast with believers explicitly described as unknown in the later scene.
The absent ally category sets the boundary: hidden believers must not be redescribed as hostile allies.
The prevention of hands supplies the overt restraint whose hidden reason is then disclosed.
Unrevealed knowledge supplies the hidden human presence that ordinary battlefield perception cannot locate.
Literal trampling supplies the collateral mechanism that blocks immediate combat.
Separation and distinction supply the unrealized condition under which delayed punishment could proceed.

structural_cues: 48:25 uses two counterfactual structures to explain why the combat counterfactual of 48:22 did not become actual.
The hidden believers occupy the same social space without being recognized by the addressed group.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies restraint, unknown believers, risk of trampling, and punishment conditional on separation; I infer that intermixture temporarily suspends the focus outcome across the whole field. A live alternative is to describe the mechanism only as protection of believers, treating any delay for their opponents as incidental rather than shielding.

changed_reading.before: The absence of ally and helper means there is nothing at all delaying the enemy's defeat.
changed_reading.after: Once combat begins no conventional support can save them, yet before combat an unseen intermixture can suspend the encounter without becoming their ally or helper.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later contrast places heated pride in the disbelievers' hearts and settled stillness upon the messenger and believers. Read back into the focus, the rout can arise from unequal cohesion: self-heating agitation drives brittle aggression, while settled hearts preserve coordinated relation. The absent wali/nasir is then partly an internal failure to sustain a support-bearing formation.

activation_trace.role: Truth-blocking resistance identifies the hostile group whose inward motive is later exposed.
Withdrawal supplies the outward motion potentially generated by inward instability.
Battlefield retreat supplies the visible failure of cohesion.
Inflamed pride and anger supply a volatile motive inside the hostile formation.
The stopping of agitation supplies the opposing formation's stabilizing affect.
The heart locates the contest of heat and stillness inside collective action rather than only in weapons.

structural_cues: 48:26 explicitly contrasts the two groups through opposed inward states soon after the focus verse.
The focus moves from combat to turning and failed support, a sequence compatible with cohesion loss.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies heated pride, settled stillness, and the same opposed groups; I supply the arrow from affective state to battlefield cohesion. A live alternative is that the states are theological characterizations with no tactical causal role.

changed_reading.before: The predicted rout follows from an unspecified superiority in force.
changed_reading.after: The rout may also expose an affective asymmetry: heated self-assertion fragments under pressure while settled relation remains capable of coordinated support.

context_deltas.mechanism: The final crop model makes support developmental rather than merely personal: a shoot emerges beside its source, is strengthened, thickens, and stands. Read back into wali/nasir, successful support is a network that produces adjacent growth and increasing load-bearing capacity. The hostile side's failure is the absence of such a self-reinforcing ecology.

activation_trace.role: Adjacency without a gap supplies the spatial relation between source plant and emerging shoot.
Effective assistance supplies the functional relation later embodied as mutual plant strengthening.
Cultivated emergence and growth supply the larger developmental system.
The shoot emerging around the origin supplies a concrete image of adjacent multiplication.
Plants becoming strong through mutual support supply the active nasr-like function.
Thickening after initial delicacy supplies the measurable result of successful support.

structural_cues: 48:29 closes the surah with a sequence of emergence, strengthening, thickening, and standing.
The crop is collective and internally reinforcing, in direct contrast to 48:22's empty search for support.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent shoots, mutual strengthening, and thickening; I infer that this is a material model for the support relations named in the focus. A live alternative is that the crop describes only the believers' growth and should not be projected back onto wali/nasir terminology.

changed_reading.before: Wali and nasir refer only to two absent rescuing individuals.
changed_reading.after: They also index a missing ecology of adjacency and reinforcement: the routed side cannot generate the networked growth that the final crop embodies.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context juxtaposes protective covering of fault with the adversarial covering of truth. This makes alladhina kafaru in the focus less static: it identifies agents committed to a covering operation whose protective capacity fails under confrontation. Their later inability to find a wali or nasir is also the failure to secure another cover against consequence.

activation_trace.role: Blocking truth supplies the adversarial covering operation that identifies the fighters.
Generic covering keeps the concrete operation audible beneath the theological designation.
Covering fault while shielding its bearer supplies a protective counterpart to truth-concealment.
Erasing bad acts by covering them demonstrates that the same root-field can name a saving rather than resistant cover.

structural_cues: Protective covering appears near the surah's opening before the focus names those who cover truth.
The same k-f-r inventory is realized with sharply different objects and agents inside the context.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies several explicit covering branches; I infer a contrast between cover that protects from fault and cover that resists truth, with confrontation exposing the latter's failure. A live alternative is to keep the derived senses separate and hear no active covering mechanism in the focus designation.

changed_reading.before: Those who disbelieved is a fixed group label unrelated to the verse's support mechanics.
changed_reading.after: The label carries a failed operation: those who cover truth cannot make that cover hold, nor find a further protective relation once aggression exposes them.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because qatalakum is grammatically anchored in reciprocal combat, while the cited q-t-l branch concerns complete epistemic mastery. It remains live because 48:21 immediately supplies total encompassing and measured governance, and the focus itself presents a confidently closed counterfactual outcome. Downstream prose should render it only as an epistemic overtone on the battle prediction, never as a replacement for fighting.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The combat verb opens an irrealis whose result is stated without uncertainty, and al-adbar can point toward the already-read consequence.

activation_trace.role: Complete mastery of a report or matter supplies the branch-distant sense that the combat outcome is already epistemically conquered.
Looking through an affair to its consequence links the battle's beginning to its already-specified end.
Complete encompassing in knowledge and possession supplies the adjacent image of an outcome already enclosed.
Measured governance supplies the ordering frame in which the counterfactual result is fixed before enactment.

changed_reading.before: The verse predicts a likely result from superior force.
changed_reading.after: As a secondary overtone, the unrealized battle is already mastered as knowledge: its consequence is enclosed and read through to the end before swords meet.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the ordinary focus sense is disbelief, not farming. It remains anchored because the focus inventory explicitly supplies seed-covering, while 48:29 places kuffar beside a detailed crop whose shoot emerges and is strengthened. Downstream prose should qualify this as deliberate or emergent root-play and ecological inversion, not translate alladhina kafaru as farmers.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Alladhina kafaru identifies the hostile side, and the same root can image the covering of seed beneath the ground.

activation_trace.role: Seed-covering supplies the latent material image inside the hostile group's designation.
The repeated designation beside the crop reactivates the seed-covering image at the point of hostile anger.
Growth from cultivation supplies what rises beyond the cover.
The new shoot emerging around its origin supplies visible life from a covered beginning.
Mutual strengthening of the plants supplies the support system the focus enemy cannot find.

changed_reading.before: The hostile group and the final crop simile occupy unrelated semantic domains.
changed_reading.after: The coverers confront a growth they cannot suppress: a covered beginning emerges, multiplies, and develops its own mutual support while their side cannot find one.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is highly branch-distant because wali and nasir in the focus most naturally denote human or divine support. It remains packet-anchored through explicit branches for following rain and rain as rescue, activated by the final crop and a rain-marking branch in its description. Downstream prose should carry it only as a cross-domain ecological shadow on support, never as the verse's primary referent.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The coordinated waliyyan wa-la nasiran can, at the edge of the supplied inventories, evoke both follow-on rain and rain that rescues a land.

activation_trace.role: Rain arriving after the first seasonal rain supplies an ecological version of support through succession.
Rain that relieves and revives a land supplies an ecological version of active rescue.
The first rain marking earth with vegetation activates the seasonal sequence behind the focus rain branches.
Cultivated growth supplies the ecological field in which rain can function as succession and rescue.

changed_reading.before: The support pair is exhausted by social and military assistance.
changed_reading.after: At the exploratory edge, the pair also casts an aridity-shadow: no succeeding rain and no reviving downpour answer the routed side, while the opposed crop receives a complete growth ecology.

strongest_changes: The repeated و ل ي root makes retreat self-canceling: turning out of relation culminates in no protective relation being found.
Opening, prevailing, and reciprocal restraint recast the battle as an unrealized capability inside a victory achieved without requiring combat.
The adjacent future-negated finding in 48:23 generalizes the absent wali and nasir into an invariant, non-substitutable pattern.
Hidden believers delay enactment of the counterfactual without becoming allies of the hostile side, while the final crop supplies a distinct model of successful mutual support.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly changed the scale of the focus reading without forcing a single resolution: body-turn became relational self-cancellation, a tactical hypothetical became restrained victory and invariant order, unseen intermixture complicated absolute abandonment, and the closing crop turned support into a developmental ecology. The epistemic, seed-covering, and rain readings remain contained but live because explicit packet branches support them.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the repeated negated finding across 48:22-23 is a designed semantic hinge or only tight verbal cohesion.
How strongly the hidden intermixture may be described as temporarily shielding the hostile group without mistaking protected believers for its wali or nasir.
How much downstream prose should surface the agricultural and rain branches rather than leave them as latent cross-domain activations.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Combat reverses into rearward motion.** `قاتلكم` anchors ق ت ل B011 (mutual combat); `لولوا` anchors و ل ي B007 (turning away), and `الأدبار` anchors د ب ر B001/B003 (back; withdrawing). The condition pivots active facing into exposed backs. I infer that the promised reversal is the operative victory mechanism. The ayah emphasizes redirected motion rather than the clash itself.
2. **No support means no operative capacity.** `يجدون` anchors و ج د B001 (finding) and B003 (capacity/means); `وليًا` anchors و ل ي B004 (loyal alliance/support), and `نصيرًا` anchors ن ص ر B001. I infer that “not finding” is institutional and causal, not merely locational: no alliance exists that can make resistance effective. Defeat is read as collapse of a support network.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 48:24 supplies a surprising correction: prevalence occurs, yet hands are restrained rather than combat completed. The hypothetical reversal in 48:22 is one possible expression of superiority, not the only one.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A counterfactual combat that exposes orientation.** Fixed `قَاتَلَكُم` anchors ق ت ل `B011`, mutual combat; `لَوَلَّوُا` anchors و ل ي `B007`, turning away, and `ٱلْأَدْبَار` anchors د ب ر `B003`, turning the back and withdrawing. Ayah 48:24 later says both sets of hands were actually restrained after capacity to prevail existed. The packet supplies hypothetical engagement and actual non-engagement; I infer **counterfactual pressure -> revealed retreat orientation even without the collision being realized**. The verse demonstrates the support relation's weakness rather than narrating a battle.

2. **No recoverable means after the turn.** Fixed `يَجِدُون` anchors و ج د `B003`, capacity, means, and wealth, alongside finding in `B001`; `وَلِيًّا` anchors و ل ي `B004`, loyal alliance and support, and `نَصِيرًا` anchors ن ص ر `B001`, aid that makes someone prevail. Ayah 48:21 has contrasted human incapacity with encompassing divine capacity. I infer **withdrawal from the field -> search for replacement support -> no effective means found**. `لَا يَجِدُون` becomes failure of support capacity, not only failure to locate a person.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Ayah 48:24 corrected a natural expectation that the counterfactual battle must be realized: hands were instead restrained after prevailing capacity existed. Ayah 48:25 supplied the protective reason, so retreat and lack of support are exposed without treating collision as the only proof.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A summons reorganizes bodies by launching them toward an encounter, resolving contact, or exposing reversal and refusal.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Remaining Behind Becomes Reversal
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Refusal leaves a party behind and then turns movement backward at the point of pressure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: those remaining behind (`quranic:root_000433:B003/m01`); turning away (`quranic:root_001684:B007/m01`); turning the back in retreat (`quranic:root_000458:B003/m01`).

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Being left behind is not only a location in the marching order. Under renewed summons it becomes an orientation: refusal turns the body away, and military retreat makes that orientation visible as the exposed back.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, canın bedenden ayrılmasına yol açan öldürme eylemini ve bu sonucu doğuran çeşitli araçları açıkça bildirir. İnsan bedeninde vurulduğunda ölüm getiren yerler de aynı çekirdeğe bağlı özel bir kullanımdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu anlam, karşılıklı savaşmayı, yalnızca ölüm tehlikesi yaratmayı ve mecazlı bilgi kullanımlarını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım temel öldürme anlamını verir; kötü biçimde öldürme ve bedendeki ölümcül noktalar yalnızca kendi kalıplarına bağlı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Canlı bir varlığın canını bedeninden ayırarak ölümüne yol açmaktır. Darbe, yara, taş, zehir ya da hastalık bu sonucu doğuran araçlardan olabilir.

facets.statement: Bir canlının yaşamını sona erdirip canını bedeninden ayırma eylemidir.
İnsan bedeninde vurulması ya da yaralanması ölüm getiren noktalar bu anlamın özel bir beden kullanımını oluşturur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, anlamın özünü canın bedenden ayrılması ve bunun sonucunda ölümün gerçekleşmesi olarak birleştirir; kullanılan araç değişse de sonuç aynıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir canlının yaşamını doğrudan sona erdiren eylemin genel ve sonuç odaklı karşılığıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Canın alınması işlemini ve ölüm sonucunu birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Araç ya da öldürme biçiminin ayrıca belirtilmediği olağan eylem bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yaşamı sona erdiren eylemi doğal Türkçeyle tam olarak karşılar.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İnsan bedeninde isabet aldığında ölüme yol açan yerlerden söz edilirken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Bedendeki ölüm getiren yerler yönünü açık biçimde korur.
error_profile.loses: Genel öldürme eylemini ve onun farklı araçlarını kapsamaz.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: onu kötü ve çirkin bir biçimde öldürme

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak anlam, bir failin yaşamı sona erdiren eylemini bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu anlam, ölüm olayını, ölü olma durumunu ya da cansız bedeni de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki anlam da canlılığın sona ermesi sonucunda buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Öldürme, sonucu doğuran eylemdir; ölüm ise bu eylemden bağımsız olarak da gerçekleşebilen olay ya da durumdur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak anlam her türlü tamamlanmış öldürmeyi kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu anlam yalnızca önceden yaralanmış birinin öldürülmesini tamamlama aşamasına özgüdür.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki anlamda da bir kişinin yaşamı bilinçli bir eylemle sona erdirilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu anlam, yaralanmış kişiye son darbeyi vurma koşulunu taşır; odak anlam böyle bir ön aşama gerektirmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak anlam, karşılıklılık gerektirmeden ölüm sonucunun gerçekleşmesini bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu anlam, iki ya da daha çok tarafın öldürme amacıyla karşılıklı çatışmasını bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki anlamda da öldürme amacı ya da ölüm olasılığı bulunabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Karşılıklı savaş ölümle sonuçlanmayabilir; öldürme ise karşılıklı bir çatışma olmadan da gerçekleşebilir ve sonucu esas alır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه القتل المعروف، إزالة الروح، القتيل والقتلى، قتلة السوء، والتكثير في القتل، وما يصيب مقاتل الإنسان فيميته.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi boyun eğdirme ve işe alıştırma çekirdeğini destekler; deneyimli kişi kullanımı ise şiddetin yumuşaması değil, işlerce sınanıp pişmiş olma sonucudur. Bu nedenle çerçeve, eğitim ile deneyim sonucunu ayırarak kullanılabilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Boyun eğdirme ve alıştırma temel kullanımdır; deneyimli kişi anlamı yalnızca belirtilen niteleme kalıbına bağlı bir uzantıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Temel edilgenleştirme ve alıştırma anlamı, hayvanın işe alışmışlığı ile insanın deneyim kazanmışlığını bildiren kalıplardan ayrı gösterilir.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanı ya da hayvanı boyun eğdirmek veya yalnız hayvan için onu işe alışır duruma getirmektir. Belirli niteleme kalıplarında, işlerce sınanarak deneyim kazanmış kimseyi de anlatır.

facets.statement: Bir insanı ya da hayvanı direnci kırılmış ve uysal duruma getirme ya da özellikle hayvanı bir işe alıştırmadır.
İnsan için kullanıldığında, birçok işle sınanmış ve deneyim kazanmış olmayı bildirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar boyun eğdirme, hayvanı işe alıştırma ve tekrar ya da sınanma yoluyla deneyimli hale gelme çizgisini birlikte gösterir.

concept_gloss.text: boyun eğdirme; hayvanı işe alıştırma; deneyimle pişme
concept_gloss.applicability: İnsan veya hayvanı boyun eğdirme, hayvanı işe alıştırma ve insanın sınanarak deneyimli hale gelme kapsamlarını ayrı ayrı özetleyen açıklayıcı karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Boyun eğdirmeyi, hayvana bağlı işe alıştırmayı ve deneyim sonucu pişmeyi ayrı kapsamlarıyla korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Özellikle bir hayvanın direncinin kırılması ve belirli bir işe alışması bağlamında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Boyun eğdirme ve düzenli işe alıştırma işlemlerini korur.
error_profile.loses: İnsan için sınanmış ve deneyimli olma uzantısını dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir insanın birçok durumla karşılaşıp bunları öğrenmiş olduğu niteleme bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Sınanma sonucunda edinilen deneyim ve ustalık yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Bir canlıyı boyun eğdirme ve işe alıştırma işlemini kapsamaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak anlam boyun eğdirme yönünü ve insan için deneyimle pişme uzantısını içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu anlam eğitim ve sık kullanım yoluyla beceri kazandırmayı daha geniş biçimde kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki anlam da bir canlıyı tekrar ve eğitimle kolay yönetilir hale getirmeyi kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odakta direncin kırılması belirgindir ve deneyimli insan uzantısı vardır; komşu anlam ise eğitme ve beceri kazandırma sürecine daha geniş yer verir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak anlam, boyun eğdirmenin yanında işe alışma ve deneyim kazanma sonucunu taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu anlam, eğitim ya da iş alışkanlığı gerektirmeyen genel bir boyun eğme durumudur.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki anlamda da direnç azalır ve uysal bir durum ortaya çıkar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Boyun eğme yalnızca tutumu veya durumu bildirir; odak anlam bu durumu yaptırma ve çalışmaya alıştırma sürecini de içerir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şey, görüş ya da haber hakkında eksiksiz bilgiye ve kesinliğe ulaşmayı açıkça anlatır. Bu kullanım fiziksel öldürmeden bağımsız, belirli söz dizimlerine bağlı bir bilme anlamıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnızca eksiksiz ve kuşku bırakmayan bilgi bağlamındadır; sıradan bilme, sanı veya fiziksel öldürme değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, bilgi veya kesinlik bildiren belirtilmiş yapıya bağlıdır ve kökün yalın anlamı gibi genelleştirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir şey, görüş ya da haber hakkında kuşku bırakmayacak ölçüde eksiksiz bilgi edinip kesinliğe ulaşmaktır.

facets.statement: Bilgi konusu olan şeyi bütünüyle kavrayıp onun hakkında kesin bilgiye sahip olmadır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, söz konusu yapıyı haber, görüş veya başka bir konu hakkında tam bilgi ve kesinlik kazanma biçiminde ortaklaşa açıklar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir konuya ilişkin bilginin hem kapsamlı hem de kuşkudan uzak olduğunu anlatan tam karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Bilginin eksiksizliğini ve kesinliğini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kesinlik bağlamdan zaten anlaşıldığında doğal ve kısa bir eylem karşılığı olarak kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Bilginin yüzeysel değil, kapsamlı ve sağlam olması yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Kuşkunun bütünüyle giderildiğini tek başına açıkça bildirmez.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: bir şeyi eksiksiz ve kesin olarak bilmek

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu anlam, kuşkunun giderildiği genel kesinlik durumunu ve buna ilişkin daha geniş türevleri kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki anlam da kuşkunun ortadan kalktığı sağlam bilgiyi bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak, bilgi nesnesini eksiksiz kavrama kalıbıdır; komşu ise herhangi bir yargının kesinleşmesini daha genel biçimde anlatır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قتل الشيء خبرا أو علما أو يقينا، أي بلوغ العلم التام والإحاطة بالرأي أو الحديث.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kadının süslenip nazlı biçimde salınmasını, kişinin işine incelikle yaklaşmasını ve bir kadına yalvarmasını aynı dönüşlü yapı çevresinde açıkça tanıklar. Bu alt kullanımlar tanımda birbirine karıştırılmadan korunabilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Nazlı yürüyüş, bir işi elde etmek için yumuşak yol arama ve bir kadına yalvarma ayrı bağlamlardır; aşk yüzünden kendinden geçme bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnızca belirtilen dönüşlü yapılarda geçerlidir; yalın köke genel bir nazlanma ya da yalvarma anlamı verilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir kadının birine hoş görünmek için süslenip nazlı biçimde salınması ve bükülmesidir. Başka yapılarda, kişinin isteğine incelikle yaklaşmasını ya da bir kadına alçalarak yalvarmasını anlatır.

facets.statement: Bir kadının hoş görünmek amacıyla süslenmesi, nazlanması ve yürürken salınıp bükülmesidir.
Bir kişinin gereksinimini elde etmek için ona incelikli ve yumuşak yollarla yaklaşmasıdır.
Bir erkeğin bir kadına kendini alçaltarak yalvarmasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar nazlı süslenme ve salınmayı ortak çekirdek olarak verir; aynı yapı, isteğe yumuşak yollarla yaklaşma ve bir kadına yalvarma bağlamlarına da uzanır.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu anlam insan ya da hayvanın yürüyüşünde, boynunda veya kalçasında yalın eğilip bükülmeyi kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki anlam bedenin yürüyüş sırasında eğilip salınması görünümünde kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bedensel bükülme tek başına naz ya da yöneltilmiş bir davranış değildir; odak anlamda bu toplumsal ve duygusal yön kurucudur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar incelendi; eşe nazlanma, yürüyüşte kırıtma ve yalın bedensel bükülme en yakın üç sınırı verdi, şiir ve alkış gibi uzak adaylar yayımlanmadı.
branches.branch_image_ar: تدلل وتكسر في مشية أو طلب
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه تقتل الجارية أو المرأة للفتى في التزين والتثني والتكسر، وتقتل الرجل لحاجته أو للمرأة بمعنى التأتي والتضرع.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه موت العشق نفسه، ولا المقاتلة بين اثنين.
branches.source_phrase_ar: تقتلت الجارية للرجل حتى عشقها كأنها خضعت له (maqayis)؛ تقتلت الجارية للفتى تزينت ومشت مشية حسنة تقلبت فيها وتثنت وتكسرت (ayn)؛ تقتل الرجل لحاجته إذا تأتى لها والرجل يتقتل للمرأة يتضرع إليها (jamhara)؛ تقتلت المرأة في مشيتها إذا تقلبت وتثنت وتكسرت (sihah)؛ معنى تقتلها وتدللها واختيالها (tahdhib)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin temel bölümü birini öldürülmeye açık hale getirmeyi doğrular. Çeneler arasındaki ölüm nedeni sözü ise doğrudan birini tehlikeye atma eylemi değil, kişinin kendi sözlerinin ölümüne neden olabileceğini belirten ayrı bir kalıptır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Tehlikeye açma temel kullanımdır; dilin ölüme neden olması yalnızca belirtilen atasözümsü kalıba bağlıdır ve gerçekleşmiş öldürme değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Öldürülme tehlikesine açık kılma ile kişinin sözünü ölüm nedeni sayan kalıp ayrı tutulur; hiçbiri doğrudan öldürme sonucuyla özdeşleştirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Birini öldürülebileceği bir duruma sokmak ya da ölümüne yol açabilecek nedeni hazırlamaktır. Özel bir kalıpta, kişinin söyledikleri kendi ölümünün nedeni sayılır.

facets.statement: Bir kişiyi başkalarınca öldürülmeye açık ve savunmasız bir duruma getirmedir.
Kişinin diliyle söylediği sözlerin kendi ölümüne neden olabileceğini bildiren kalıplaşmış bir kullanımdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar birini ölüm tehlikesine açık bırakmayı ortak biçimde tanıklar; ayrıca kişinin dilini ve sözünü kendi ölümünün nedeni sayan kalıplaşmış bir anlatım verir.

concept_gloss.text: öldürülmeye açık kılma veya ölüm nedeni hazırlama
concept_gloss.applicability: Gerçekleşmiş ölümden önceki tehlikeye sokma işlemini ve kalıplaşmış neden bildirimini birlikte kapsar.

error_profile.preserves: Tehlikeye açık kılma ile ölüm nedenini hazırlama yönlerini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin başkalarınca öldürülebileceği koşullara bilerek veya neden olarak sokulduğu bağlamda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişiyi ölüm tehlikesine açık hale getirme işlemini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin söylediği sözlerin başına ölümcül bir sonuç getirebileceğini anlatan özdeyiş bağlamındadır.

error_profile.loses: Başkasını öldürülme tehlikesine sokan genel eylemi kapsamaz.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Birini öldürülmeye açık kılmak yalnızca koşulu yaratır; öldürme ise bu olasılığın gerçekleşmiş sonucudur.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Korumasızlık genel bir ele geçirilme açıklığıdır; odak anlam bu açıklığı özellikle öldürülme sonucuna bağlar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak anlam öldürülmeye açık hale getirmeyi bildirir ve gizlilik gerektirmez.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu anlam fark ettirmeden ele geçirip gerçekten yok etme ya da öldürme eylemidir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki anlam da bir kişinin savunmasızlığından ölümcül sonuç doğması alanına girer.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Gizlice öldürmede ölümcül eylem tamamlanır ve fark edilmeme belirleyicidir; odakta yalnızca tehlikeli koşul veya neden hazırlanabilir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; tamamlanmış öldürme, korumasızlık ve gizli öldürme, tehlikeye açma çekirdeğinin en yararlı üç sınırını sağladı.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi aşkın ya da görünmeyen varlıkların kişiyi veya yüreğini yenip aklını bozacak ölçüde etkisi altına almasını açıkça tanıklar. Kullanım yalnızca bu iki etkene bağlanan mecazlı bir yenilgi durumudur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal fiziksel ölümü veya birine hoş görünmek için nazlanmayı değil, aşk ya da görünmeyen varlıklar yüzünden ağır biçimde yenik düşmeyi anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yüreğin aşka yenilmesi kalıbı ile kişinin aşk ya da görünmeyen varlıklar yüzünden aklının karışması ayrı yapılara bağlı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Aşkın kişinin yüreğine bütünüyle üstün gelmesidir. Ayrı bir yapıda, aşkın ya da görünmeyen varlıkların kişinin aklını bozacak veya onu kendinden geçirecek ölçüde yenmesini anlatır.

facets.statement: Aşkın kişinin yüreğini güçsüz bırakıp ona bütünüyle üstün gelmesidir.
Aşkın ya da görünmeyen varlıkların etkisiyle kişinin aklının karışması ve kendinden geçmesidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar aşkın yüreğe üstün gelmesini ve aşk ya da görünmeyen varlıkların kişiyi aklı karışmış duruma sokmasını, öldürmeye benzetilen ağır bir yenilgi olarak sunar.

concept_gloss.text: aşka yenik düşmüş yürek; aşk veya görünmeyen varlıklar yüzünden aklın bozulması
concept_gloss.applicability: Aşkın yüreğe üstün gelmesi ile ayrı yapıdaki aşk veya görünmeyen varlık kaynaklı akıl bozulmasını kendi kapsamlarında karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Yüreğin aşka yenilmesini ve aşk ya da görünmeyen varlıkların aklı bozması sonucunu ayrı kapsamlarıyla korur.

error_profile.loses: Görünmeyen varlıkların etkisini ve kişinin aklının bozulması kullanımını bütünüyle kapsamaz.

contextual_glosses.text: aşk ya da görünmeyen varlıklar yüzünden aklı karışmak
contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin bu iki etkenden biri nedeniyle kendinden geçip sağlıklı düşünemez hale geldiği bağlamdadır.

error_profile.preserves: Sınırlı nedenleri ve aklın ağır biçimde etkilenmesi sonucunu birlikte korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak anlam aşk ya da görünmeyen varlıkların kişiyi aklı bozulacak ölçüde yenmesini zorunlu kılar.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki anlam aşkın kişiyi olağan düşünce ve davranış çizgisinden çıkarmasında kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Başıboş dolaşma davranış sonucunu öne çıkarır; odak anlam ise etkenin kişiye üstün gelip aklını bozmasını tanımlar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak anlam aşkı da neden olarak içerir ve ağır bir yenilgi ya da kendinden geçme bildirir.

branches.branch_image_ar: قهر العشق أو الجن كقتل معنوي
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قلب مقتل قتله العشق، واقتتل الرجل إذا غلبه عشق النساء أو الجن وخبلوه.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه تزين المرأة وتكسرها نفسه، ولا القتل الحسي.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi belirli içkiyi suyla karıştırıp sertliğini gidermeyi açıkça tanımlar. Burada kurucu sonuç yalnız karışma değil, su eklenmesiyle içkinin gücünün kırılmasıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnızca içki ile su kalıbına bağlıdır; genel karıştırma, başka içecekler veya canlı öldürme anlamına genişletilemez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnızca içkinin suyla karıştırılması kalıbına bağlı tutulur ve yalın kök anlamı olarak sunulmaz.

concept_map.definition: İçkiye su katıp onu karıştırarak sertliğini ve etkisini azaltmaktır.

facets.statement: İçkiye su ekleyip karıştırma yoluyla onun sertliğini gidermedir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar içkinin suyla karıştırılmasını ortaklaşa verir; ayrıntılı açıklama, bu işlemin içkinin sertliğini giderip onu yumuşattığını belirtir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnızca belirtilen içki ve su yapısında, hem karıştırma işlemini hem de gücün azalması sonucunu karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Suyla karıştırma aracını ve sertliği giderme sonucunu birlikte korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi sözcüğü hem düşman hem de karşısındaki denk kişi ya da rakip için tanıklar. Bu iki yön karşı karşıya durma ortaklığında birleşse de her denk kişinin düşman olmadığı tanımda açık tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal bir eylemi değil karşıda duran kişiyi adlandırır; düşmanlık ve denklik alternatif yönlerdir, birbirinin zorunlu koşulu değildir.
